title: Autograd gradient count follows actual apply arguments, not forward defaults
applies_when: A torch.autograd.Function backward hypothesis counts the forward signature's optional arguments, especially a Float8Tensor SplitAlongDim path with squeeze=False.
lesson: Inspect actual Function.apply call sites before declaring a gradient-count bug. An omitted Python default is not an additional autograd input. The PyTorch engine compares backward results against the arguments supplied to apply; it also discards extra trailing None results. TransformerEngine's multi-head-attention calls supply three arguments even though forward declares a fourth optional squeeze argument. Therefore the alleged unconditional four-versus-three failure does not follow for those callers. A small native Torch control can test this mechanism cheaply before building the operator environment.
avoid_when: Explicitly passing False or True does add an input and may require another backward result. This observation must not reject all four-argument concerns. Trace requires_grad, the actual gradient subclass and squeezed shape before reproducing that path. A generic Torch control does not execute TransformerEngine, its Float8Tensor storage branch, attention kernels or numerical reference, and does not prove those paths correct.

evidence.note: The engine uses is_variable_input.size() as the expected result count, permits excess results only when all excess entries are None, and rejects remaining mismatches (lines 172-199). Public engine mechanism, not operator qualification.

The packed-QKV caller supplies only mixed_x_layer, split_dim and sections; the mixed-KV caller at lines 1122-1126 also supplies three inputs. Static counterevidence to counting an omitted squeeze default.

A separate dequantization helper explicitly passes True as a fourth argument. Its reachability and gradient-shape contract remain separate questions; it must not be covered by a blanket no-bug conclusion.
